extracted.intended_audience: general readers; philanthropists; trustees and civic leaders
extracted.subtask_description: Implicit guidance and evaluative criteria for making and administering major philanthropic gifts (organ grants, pension funds, public parks, Peace Palace), selecting beneficiaries and trustees, and for practical peace-making and public-speaking conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organ department giving policy
rubrics_metrics.description: A printed schedule requiring answers must be filled and returned before action is taken; gifts are 'graduated' according to the size of the church; congregations are required to pay one half of the desired new organ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rigid system systematizes giving so the department 'works admirably' and ensures congregational investment, preventing wasteful spending. It arose after criticism (e.g., strict Presbyterians) and the payer-participation rule ('partner in my sin') both justified the practice and sustained demand for better instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pension fund beneficiary criteria and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Private pension fund placements are limited to persons 'whom you have long known to be kind and good and in every way deserving' and 'Not one person have I ever placed upon the pension list that did not fully deserve assistance.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modest sums insure comfortable circumstances in old age; the fund is administered with strict privacy—'There is no publicity about it. No one knows who is embraced. Not a word is ever breathed to others.' The fund's moral aim is to relieve deserving aged persons from solicitude for maintenance rather than public recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeting pension funds to former employees and widows
rubrics_metrics.description: Railroad Pension Fund and similar funds benefit 'the worthy railroad men who served under me ... or their widows' and many are those the donor 'had known personally.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal acquaintance and service under the donor are highlighted as reasons for selection, reflecting loyalty and gratitude to past associates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large-scale pension endowments for broader worker cohorts
rubrics_metrics.description: The four-million-dollar Steel Workers' Pensions fund 'embraces hundreds that I never saw' yet still binds the donor because some beneficiaries are personally remembered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when beneficiaries are largely anonymous, large funds can be justified and emotionally engaged via connections to remembered individuals among the beneficiaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust deed objectives for Pittencrieff Park (verbatim success criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: To bring into the monotonous lives of the toiling masses of Dunfermline, more 'of sweetness and light,' to give to them--especially the young--some charm, some happiness, some elevating conditions of life which residence elsewhere would have denied, that the child of my native town, looking back in after years, however far from home it may have roamed, will feel that simply by virtue of being such, life has been made happier and better.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The trustees' success is explicitly measured by whether the Park produces these social and moral effects; if this is achieved they 'will have succeeded; if not, you will have failed.' The passage is offered as a concrete, quoted rubric for civic-park philanthropy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trustee selection and endowment practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Trustees should be 'public-spirited citizens' chosen to manage a donated park; the gift included a large endowment (half a million sterling in bonds bearing five per cent interest) for the town's benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection of trustees may be handled discreetly; the donor organized and invited certain men to form trusteeship and provided permanent funding to secure the park's long-term administration in line with the trust deed's aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition precedent for major civic donations to foreign governments
rubrics_metrics.description: The donor required that the Government of the Netherlands formally request and indicate desire for a Temple of Peace at The Hague before he would furnish means; drafts from the government would be honored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes a precedent: large international gifts should be made in response to an official governmental request rather than unilaterally; the donor preferred deference to governmental initiative and formal channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for institutional peace mechanisms as highest peace objective
rubrics_metrics.description: The creation of a permanent tribunal/International Court to settle international disputes is presented as 'the greatest step toward peace that humanity had ever taken' and as the measure by which the abolition of war will be judged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institution-building (a high court or permanent tribunal) is prioritized over disarmament as the practical path toward sustained international peace; advocacy and funding for such institutions are framed as the highest philanthropic contribution to peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical peace-making through social proximity
rubrics_metrics.description: If you wish to play peace-maker, seat adversaries next each other where they must begin by being civil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical anecdote: deliberately seating opponents together at dinner can force civility and sometimes resolve disputes, because 'we only hate those whom we do not know.' This is offered as a practical tactic for reconciliation and local peacemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improving public-speaking effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: A lecturer who 'was not heard' should 'fit himself for public speaking' by taking elocution lessons on a few points; being 'too ministerial' in manner reduces effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific remedial advice: engage an elocutionist for targeted lessons, correct ministerial tone, and practice projection and delivery; such adjustments enabled Matthew Arnold to fill a larger hall subsequently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical standard for personal financial responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Not what I owe to my creditors, but what I owe to myself is the issue.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As exemplified by Mark Twain's reaction to bankruptcy and by Carnegie's praise, moral character is demonstrated by choosing the harder path of repaying debts fully rather than taking the legally easier route—an ethical rubric for personal conduct relevant to benefactors and public figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design and management of literary and social philanthropic events
rubrics_metrics.description: Literary dinners and similar gatherings should be managed with thoughtful seating, appropriate quotations on cards, and opportunities for novitiate speeches to create engagement and conviviality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: use a manager to arrange devices and quotations that cause 'hilarity'; separate potential antagonists only when necessary, but sometimes reconciling them by deliberate seating is preferred. Such event design promotes community among beneficiaries and supporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach to honors and public recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept honors humbly; they 'humble, they do not exalt; so let them come' and should remind the recipient to 'strive harder than ever' and to watch acts and words closely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public decorations should be treated as reminders of responsibility rather than as personal elevation; recipients ought to respond with continued effort toward the ideals for which the honor was given.
